# Semantic-Anchor Checkpoints (SAC) for Suffix-Only Re-Prefill under a Code-as-Law Invariant Lattice

## 0. Definitions

**D1 — Context tree.** The agent's context is a tree `T` of nodes (`SESSION → TURN → MESSAGE → PART_{TEXT|TOOL_CALL|TOOL_RESULT|SUMMARY|POLICY_PIN}`). Each node has a stable id, a kind, and a canonical payload (JCS-JSON/CBOR bytes).

**D2 — Canonical linearization.** `L(T)` is the exact token sequence sent to the model: a deterministic depth-first emission of node frames (role headers, delimiters) derived **only from content fields, never from volatile metadata** (ids, timestamps). Maintain tables `node_start[n], node_end[n]` mapping nodes to token offsets in `L(T)`.

**D3 — Invariant (law).** An invariant is versioned, deterministic, sandboxed executable code: `i = (inv_id, version, guard, code, readset, severity)` where `guard` selects a node set `scope(i) ⊆ nodes(T)` (path-glob/tag/kind selector), `code: SubgraphView × EnvView → {PASS, FAIL}`, `readset` is a declared set of additional token regions the predicate reads, `severity ∈ {HARD, SOFT}`. Deploy-time enforcement: the sandbox runs `code` against a taint-recording proxy; the recorded access set must be a subset of `scope ∪ readset`, else deployment is refused. Non-declared access = illegal law.

**D4 — Invariant lattice.** Order invariants by `(S,P) ≤ (S′,P′) ⟺ S ⊆ S′ ∧ (P′ ⟹ P on S′)`. Meet = `(S∩S′, P∧P′)`; join = `(S∪S′, P∨P′)`; top = `(all nodes, True)`; bottom = `(∅, True)`. The Hasse diagram is materialized at deploy time (scope-subset check + implication discharge by solver or by construction from a compositional DSL). Consequence used later: **verdicts propagate downward** (passing a dominating invariant implies passing everything below it); **failures propagate upward**.

**D5 — Semantic-anchor checkpoint.** A record minted at a semantic boundary of `L(T)`:

```
SAC := ⟨ anchor_id, tok_offset o, block_aligned_off ⌊o/B⌋·B, kind,
         prefix_hash, kv_handle, cert, parent_anchor_id, evict_class ⟩
```

`kind ∈ {SESSION_INIT, TURN_START, MESSAGE_BOUNDARY, TOOL_CALL_PRE, TOOL_RESULT_POST, DOC_SECTION, COMPACTION_SEAM, ROLLBACK_SEAM, LATTICE_MILESTONE}`. `prefix_hash = SHA256(canon(L(T)[0:⌊o/B⌋·B]))`, chained per block: `H_k = SHA256(H_{k−1} ‖ bytes(token_ids_k))` — identical keying to the engine's radix/prefix cache. `cert` = `{(inv_id, inv_version, verdict, evidence_digest)}` for all invariants with `tokens(scope(i)) ∩ [0,o) ≠ ∅`. `LATTICE_MILESTONE` is minted whenever the set of applicable HARD invariants changes, and pins `lattice_state_hash` for audit replay.

**D6 — Anchor Soundness Condition (ASC).** Anchor `a` at offset `o` is reusable for a new context `T′` iff `L(T′)[0:o] = L(T)[0:o]` byte-for-byte and the engine's attention mechanism at every position `< o` depends only on tokens `[0:o)` (sliding-window engines: `o` must sit inside the honest window; otherwise the anchor is invalid at mint time).

**D7 — Survival.** Given edit-produced `T′` with `p = |LCP(L(T), L(T′))|` (longest common token prefix):

```
alive(a)  ⟺  a.block_aligned_off ≤ ⌊p/B⌋·B
best      = argmax{ a.block_aligned_off : alive(a) }
recert    = { i : tokens(scope(i) ∪ readset(i)) ∩ [p, max(|L(T)|,|L(T′)|)) ≠ ∅ }
```

Only `best`'s KV is reused; `[best.block_aligned_off, |L(T′)|)` is the re-prefilled suffix. "Only the new suffix" is achieved exactly when edits land on semantic seams, because then `p` coincides with an anchor offset.

## 1. Schema

```proto
message ContextNode {
  string node_id;                 // UUIDv7, excluded from L(T)
  NodeKind kind;
  repeated ContextNode children;
  bytes  payload_canon;           // JCS/CBOR
  map<string,string> meta;        // tool_name, schema_version pin, ...
}

message Invariant {
  string inv_id;  string version;
  string expr_lang;               // "cel-v0" | "wasm-poli" | "py-sandbox"
  bytes  code;                    // (SubgraphView, EnvView) -> Verdict
  Guard  guard;                   // scope selector
  repeated RegionRef readset;     // declared extra reads (dirty tracking)
  Severity severity;              // HARD | SOFT
}

message Anchor {
  string anchor_id;               // ULID
  uint64 tok_offset;
  uint64 block_aligned_off;
  AnchorKind kind;
  bytes  prefix_hash;             // chained SHA-256, radix-compatible
  KVHandle kv;                    // {radix_key, block_ids[], device, refcount}
  CertBlock cert;
  string parent_anchor_id;
  uint64 created_at_ms;
  EvictionClass evict_class;      // PINNED | KEEP_LAST_K | EPHEMERAL
}

message CertEntry {
  string inv_id; string inv_version;
  Verdict verdict;                // PASS | PASS_ASSUME | FAIL
  bytes  evidence_digest;         // SHA-256 over exact predicate inputs
}

message EditEvent {
  string edit_id;
  EditKind kind;                  // APPEND | INSERT_AT_NODE | REPLACE_NODE
                                  // | DELETE_RANGE | COMPACT | ROLLBACK_TO_ANCHOR
  string target_node_id;          // structural edit point (never raw offsets)
  bytes  new_payload;
  string author;                  // user | agent | compactor | policy-engine
}

message PrefillPlan {
  string anchor_id;
  uint64 reuse_tokens;            // [0, reuse_tokens) served from KV
  bytes  suffix_token_ids;        // [reuse_tokens, end)
  repeated string recert_inv_ids;
  bool   hard_fail;               // true => abort, trigger rollback
}
```

## 2. Algorithms

### A1 — Minting (runs after every append / tool result / turn close)

```
mint(T, prev_anchor):
  candidates = semantic node boundaries in L(T) past prev_anchor.tok_offset
  for o in candidates:
    gain = ⌊o/B⌋·B − prev_anchor.block_aligned_off
    always = kind(o) ∈ {TOOL_RESULT_POST, COMPACTION_SEAM, LATTICE_MILESTONE}
    if gain == 0 and not always: continue        # zero KV gain, skip
    if gain < δ_min and not always: continue     # churn control
    o_b = ⌊o/B⌋·B
    h    = chain_hash(prev_anchor.prefix_hash, tokens[prev.o_b : o_b])
    kv   = engine.radix_lookup_or_insert(h, block_ids)   # refcount++
    dirty = { i : tokens(scope(i) ∪ readset(i)) ∩ [prev.tok_offset, o) ≠ ∅ }
    tops  = maximal_elements(dirty) under lattice order
    verdicts = { run(i, T) : i ∈ tops }          # propagate down Hasse diagram
    if any HARD FAIL: raise LAW_VIOLATION → A4
    cert = prev_anchor.cert \ dirty  ∪  {(i, v, evidence_digest) : i ∈ tops ↓}
    emit Anchor(o, o_b, kind(o), h, kv, cert, parent=prev_anchor.id)
    prev_anchor = that anchor
```

Cost per mint: `O(|dirty|)` predicate evaluations, never `O(|I|)`.

### A2 — Edit ingestion and survival

```
on EditEvent e:
  T′ = apply(e, T)
  # Fast path: e targets node n ⇒ p = node_start[n] (frames are content-only,
  # so untouched nodes serialize identically). General path: block-hash binary
  # search over anchors, O(log A) comparisons; verify final boundary block bytes.
  p    = |LCP(L(T), L(T′))|
  p_b  = ⌊p/B⌋·B
  best = argmax{ a.block_aligned_off : a.block_aligned_off ≤ p_b }
  dead = Anchors \ { a : a.block_aligned_off ≤ p_b }
  R_dirty = [p, max(|L(T)|, |L(T′)|))
  recert  = { i : tokens(scope(i) ∪ readset(i)) ∩ R_dirty ≠ ∅ }
  tops    = maximal_elements(recert)
  verdicts = { run(i, T′) : i ∈ tops }; propagate down
  if any HARD FAIL on T′:
      policy_dispatch(e): REJECT_EDIT (restore T) | QUARANTINE + A4 rollback
  else:
      emit PrefillPlan(best, suffix = tokens[p_b:], recert)
      free(dead.kv_handles) subject to cross-session refcounts
  T ← T′
```

Special cases, handled exactly:
- **APPEND:** `p = |L(T)|`; all anchors alive; `best` = newest; suffix = delta only. Hot path: per-turn cost `O(new tokens)`.
- **COMPACT:** modeled as `REPLACE(range [c₀,c₁) → SUMMARY node)`. Anchors in `[c₀,c₁)` die; a `COMPACTION_SEAM` anchor is minted at `c₀` with summary-fidelity laws (every open tool contract referenced, pinned schema versions carried forward).
- **ROLLBACK_TO_ANCHOR(a):** `T′ = T` truncated at `a`'s node boundary; `p = a.block_aligned_off`; everything after dies; regeneration is the suffix.

### A3 — Re-prefill

```
execute(plan):
  req.tokens       = L(T′)
  req.cache_prefix = plan.anchor.kv          # engine resumes attention here
  req.prefill_span = [plan.reuse_tokens, |req.tokens|)
  out = engine.decode(req)
  A1_mint over the new suffix, seeding cert base from
      plan.anchor.cert − recert_entries + fresh verdicts
```

### A4 — Rollback (law wins)

On HARD failure mid-generation: truncate to the newest anchor whose cert is fully green, emit `ROLLBACK_TO_ANCHOR`, regenerate through A3. The violating edit/generation is logged with evidence digests; SOFT failures log only.

## 3. Correctness (three lemmas, stated exactly)

**L1 (Reuse soundness).** Transformer KV for positions `[0,o)` is a pure function of token ids `[0,o)`. ASC guarantees byte-identical prefixes; decoding params do not affect prefill KV. Therefore serving `[0,best.block_aligned_off)` from cache is bit-equivalent to recomputation.

**L2 (Certificate inheritance).** If `i ∉ recert`, then `(scope(i) ∪ readset(i)) ∩ R_dirty = ∅`, so every input `code(i)` consumes is byte-identical in `T′`; predicates are deterministic and versioned, so the verdict and evidence digest carry over verbatim. Anything non-deterministic (clock, RNG, network) must be declared in `readset` as an `EnvRegion` or the entry is forced to `PASS_ASSUME` with a TTL.

**L3 (Lattice completeness).** Evaluating only maximal elements of `recert` suffices: by D4, a pass on a dominating invariant implies passes on everything below it; a fail propagates upward and forces re-evaluation of its joins. Total per-edit cost: `O(|Δ|)` prefill FLOPs + `O(|maximal(recert)|)` predicate runs + `O(log A)` hash comparisons.

## 4. Parameters and failure handling

| Parameter | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Block size `B` | 16 tokens | Engine parameter (vLLM-class); all offsets block-aligned |
| `δ_min` | 512 tokens | Skipped unless `always`-mint kind |
| Keep-last-K | K=4 per kind | `PINNED` (session init, policy pins) and `LATTICE_MILESTONE` kept for session lifetime |
| Hash | Chained SHA-256 per block | Radix-key compatible; final boundary block byte-verified |

Failure modes, each with a defined behavior: engine cache eviction (radix miss on `kv_handle` ⇒ fall back to next-lower live anchor, else cold prefill); tokenizer version drift (anchor stores `tokenizer_version`; mismatch ⇒ all anchors void); sliding-window attention (anchors outside the honest window refused at mint); hash collision (negligible; boundary-block byte check closes it); undeclared predicate reads (refused at deploy by taint-diff, per D3).

The design point in one sentence: **anchors are placed where edits actually land (semantic seams), survival is decided by content hashes (byte-exact, mechanically checkable), and the lattice converts "re-verify everything" into "verify the maximal dirty laws, inherit the rest" — so an edit costs exactly its suffix.**

The lattice gives a partial order over invariant scopes; each checkpoint must satisfy all invariants whose scope dominates it; violations force re-anchoring or rollback.

### Background mechanics

LLM serving engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) support **prefix caching / radix attention**: KV blocks keyed by content-addressed hashes of token prefixes. If a new request's token sequence shares a prefix with a cached sequence, those KV blocks are reused without recomputation. Block granularity matters: typically fixed-size blocks (e.g., 16 tokens). A single token change at position p invalidates all blocks containing or after p (with standard block hashing where block i's key = H(block_{i-1} key || block tokens)). So reuse length = floor(p / B) * B roughly, minus alignment issues.

Therefore: to guarantee "re-prefill only the new suffix," we need:
1. Edits to be **suffix-localized relative to some anchor**: there exists an anchor A at token offset o such that tokens [0, o) are byte-identical before and after the edit.
2. The engine's cache to retain KV for [0, o) (block-aligned: o must be a multiple of block size B, or we accept truncation to floor(o/B)*B).
3. The post-edit sequence to be [0, o) + new suffix S', with S' re-prefilled.

But raw byte-prefix identity is too weak a notion of "semantic anchor": we want anchors at *semantic* boundaries (message boundaries, tool-call/result boundaries, document section boundaries, AST node boundaries in code contexts) because:
- Semantic boundaries are stable under upstream edits that don't cross them (e.g., editing one message doesn't change earlier messages).
- They carry invariant obligations: e.g., "every tool_call has a matching tool_result," "no PII in context," "schema version pinned."

### The code-as-law invariant lattice

Define a set of invariants I, each an executable predicate (code) over a context state σ (the structured context object) plus environment E (tool registry, schemas, policies). Each invariant has a **scope** — a region of the context it governs. Scopes form a lattice under inclusion (subset order on token ranges / structural paths):

- Top element ⊤ = whole session scope.
- Bottom ⊥ = empty scope (vacuously true everywhere).
- Meet (∧) = intersection of scopes; Join (∨) = union... wait, actually for *governance*, the natural order is: invariant i₁ ≤ i₂ if scope(i₁) ⊆ scope(i₂)? Or the reverse? Let me think.

Actually more useful: think of the lattice over **checkpoint obligation sets**. At any anchor a, the applicable invariant set is Inv(a) = { i ∈ I : scope(i) ∩ region(a) ≠ ∅ } or better { i : scope(i) ⊇ prefix(a) }... Hmm. Let me define cleanly:

Let the context be a tree T (messages, parts, tool calls/results nested). Each node n has a path π(n). An invariant i declares a **guard pattern** g_i selecting nodes (e.g., `type == 'tool_result'`, or `path matches /session/messages/*`), and a predicate P_i over the selected subgraph plus ambient env. The **scope** of i is the set of nodes matching g_i.

Lattice: define partial order on invariants by scope containment: i ≤ j iff scope(i) ⊆ scope(j). Then:
- Global invariants (whole-tree guards) are top elements.
- Narrow invariants (single tool result) are bottom-ish.
- Join i ∨ j = invariant with guard g_i ∪ g_j and predicate P_i ∧ P_j (must hold wherever either applies)... hmm, careful: join should be the least upper bound. If we take join's scope = scope(i) ∪ scope(j) and predicate = P_i ∧ P_j restricted appropriately... Actually the cleanest formalization: an invariant is a pair (S, P) where S ⊆ Nodes(T) and P: Subgraph(S) × Env → Bool. Order: (S₁,P₁) ≤ (S₂,P₂) iff S₁ ⊆ S₂ and P₂ ⟹ P₁ on S₂ (stronger invariant on smaller scope is below). Then meet = (S₁∩S₂, P₁∧P₂), join = (S₁∪S₂, P₁∨P₂)? Hmm wait, but "code-as-law" suggests something stronger: invariants are *executable code* attached to the lattice, and every state transition (context edit) must be proven/certified to preserve all invariants whose scope intersects the changed region. The lattice then enables **incremental verification**: an edit touching region R only requires re-checking invariants i with scope(i) ∩ R ≠ ∅ (a "dirty-scope" propagation), plus invariants whose predicates depend on cross-region data (declared dependencies). To keep it sound, each invariant declares its **read set** (which regions its predicate reads); an edit dirties invariant i iff R ∩ (scope(i) ∪ readset(i)) ≠ ∅. That's the classic incremental view maintenance condition.

And the lattice gives monotonicity: if invariant i is certified at anchor a, and j ≤ i (j stronger/narrower), certification composes. Actually the useful property: **anchor certification is upward-closed**: certifying all maximal invariants covering a region implies all below. So at each anchor we store the certificate for the join of all dirty-relevant invariants, or per-invariant certs.

### Semantic-anchor checkpoint definition

A **semantic-anchor checkpoint** (SAC) is a record:

SAC := ⟨ aid, pos, kind, prefix_hash, kv_handle, inv_cert, ttl_policy, parent_aid ⟩

- `aid`: unique anchor id.
- `pos`: token offset o in the linearized context stream L(T) (canonical serialization of context tree T into the exact token sequence sent to the model).
- `kind`: boundary class ∈ {SESSION_INIT, TURN_START, MESSAGE_BOUNDARY, TOOL_CALL_PRE, TOOL_RESULT_POST, DOC_SECTION, COMPACTION_SEAM, USER_EDIT_SEAM, INVARIANT_LATTICE_MILESTONE}.
- `prefix_hash`: h = SHA-256(canonical_bytes(L(T)[0:o])) — content address enabling cache hit verification.
- `kv_handle`: opaque reference to cached KV blocks covering [0, o) in the serving engine's radix tree (block-aligned: covers [0, ⌊o/B⌋·B)).
- `inv_cert`: certificate C(o) = { (i_id, verdict, evidence_digest) : i ∈ ApplicableInv(o) } where ApplicableInv(o) = { i : scope(i) ∩ [0,o) ≠ ∅ } evaluated on the prefix state; verdict ∈ {PASS, PASS_WITH_ASSUMPTIONS}; evidence digest binds the check to specific input bytes (reproducibility).
- `parent_aid`: the anchor this was derived from (for chain-of-custody / audit).
- `ttl_policy`: eviction rules (e.g., keep last K anchors per kind, keep all INVARIANT_LATTICE_MILESTONE).

Key property (the **Anchor Soundness Condition**, ASC): anchor a at offset o is *reusable* for a new context T′ iff:
1. L(T′)[0:o] = L(T)[0:o] byte-for-byte (prefix stability), AND
2. Every invariant i with readset(i) ∩ [o, |L(T′)|) ≠ ∅ ... hmm no. Let me get this right.

For cache reuse we need the *common prefix* [0,p) to be intact. Any anchor with pos ≤ p (and block-aligned coverage) survives. Anchors beyond p are dead unless the edit is a pure insertion/deletion at a point where downstream content is unchanged — but even then, KV positions shift, so positional caches die; only content-addressed schemes survive, and standard KV caches are positional → any edit strictly inside kills everything after. Hence: **only anchors at pos ≤ p survive**, where p = length of longest common token prefix. That's the honest mechanical truth. Semantic anchoring maximizes the chance that p lands exactly on a semantic boundary (because edits are applied at semantic seams), and canonical serialization ensures identical semantics ⇒ identical bytes ⇒ longer common prefixes than naive serialization would give.

The optimization is: reuse [0, p_edit) where p_edit = end of last intact anchor ≤ first-difference. So the system wants anchors densely enough that p_edit coincides with an anchor, and the claim "only the new suffix is re-prefilled" means: recompute exactly [p_anchor, |L(T′)|) where p_anchor = max{ pos(a) : a alive, pos(a) ≤ p_diff, block-aligned }. Everything before is served from KV cache. 

Also need **invariant re-certification**: invariants whose readset intersects the changed region [p_diff, ...) must be re-evaluated; invariants fully contained in the intact prefix keep their certificates (that's the lattice's payoff — incremental re-verification). New suffix gets fresh anchors with fresh certs.

There's also the **compaction seam** case: compaction replaces a range [c₀, c₁) with a summary token span. Then the common prefix is [0, c₀). Anchors ≥ c₀ die; a COMPACTION_SEAM anchor is minted at c₀ with cert covering the summary's fidelity obligations (e.g., "summary preserves all open tool contracts" — an invariant in the lattice).

### Schema

I'll write it as a concrete IDL (protobuf-style or TypeScript-ish). Let me do a compact but complete schema:

```proto
// ---- Canonical context & linearization ----
message ContextNode {
  string node_id;            // stable UUIDv7
  NodeKind kind;             // SESSION | TURN | MESSAGE | PART_TEXT | PART_TOOL_CALL
                             // | PART_TOOL_RESULT | DOC_SECTION | SUMMARY | POLICY_PIN
  repeated ContextNode children;
  bytes payload_canon;       // canonical-encoded payload (JCS JSON / CBOR)
  map<string,string> meta;   // e.g. tool_name, schema_version pin
}

// ---- Invariant lattice ----
message Invariant {
  string inv_id;
  string expr_lang;          // "cel-v0" | "wasm-poli" | "py-sandbox"
  bytes  code;               // executable predicate: (SubgraphView, EnvView) -> Verdict
  Guard  guard;              // selects scope nodes
  repeated RegionRef readset;// declared extra regions read (for dirty tracking)
  Severity severity;         // HARD (violation blocks) | SOFT (logs)
  string version;
}
message Guard {
  oneof sel {
    PathGlob path;           // e.g. "/turns/*/messages/*/parts[type=TOOL_CALL]"
    TagSet tags;
    KindSet kinds;
  }
}

// Lattice ops are computed, not stored: order (S1,P1) <= (S2,P2) iff S1⊆S2 ∧ (P2⟹P1 on S2).
// Stored: the Hasse diagram edges materialized at deploy time via scope-subset + implication checks
// (implication discharged by solver or by construction from a compositional DSL).

// ---- Anchor ----
message Anchor {
  string anchor_id;          // ULID
  uint64 tok_offset;         // o, in tokens of L(T)
  uint64 block_aligned_off;  // ⌊o/B⌋·B
  AnchorKind kind;
  bytes  prefix_hash;        // SHA256(canon(L(T)[0:block_aligned_off]))
  KVHandle kv;               // engine-specific: {radix_key, block_ids[], device}
  CertBlock cert;            // invariant certificates valid on [0,o)
  string parent_anchor_id;
  uint64 created_at_ms;
  EvictionClass evict_class; // PINNED | KEEP_LAST_K | EPHEMERAL
}

message CertBlock {
  repeated CertEntry entries;
  bytes lattice_state_hash;  // hash of applicable-invariant set + versions at mint time
}
message CertEntry {
  string inv_id; string inv_version;
  Verdict verdict;           // PASS | PASS_ASSUME | FAIL(severity decides)
  bytes evidence_digest;     // SHA256 over inputs the predicate consumed
}

// ---- Edit event ----
message EditEvent {
  string edit_id;
  EditKind kind;             // APPEND | INSERT_AT_NODE | REPLACE_NODE | DELETE_RANGE | COMPACT | ROLLBACK_TO_ANCHOR
  string target_node_id;     // structural edit point (preferred over token offsets)
  bytes new_payload;         // for replace/insert
  string author;             // "user" | "agent" | "compactor" | "policy-engine"
}

// ---- Re-prefill plan ----
message PrefillPlan {
  string anchor_id;          // reuse root
  uint64 reuse_tokens;       // [0, reuse_tokens) from KV
  bytes  suffix_tokens;      // token ids for [reuse_tokens, end)
  repeated string recert_inv_ids; // invariants to re-run
  bool   hard_fail;          // any HARD invariant failed -> abort prefill
}
```

### Algorithm

Three phases: (1) anchor placement/minting during normal generation; (2) edit ingestion → survival computation; (3) re-prefill + recertification + re-minting.

**Phase 0 — Canonical linearization.** Define L(T): depth-first walk of T emitting per-node framing tokens (role headers, delimiters) deterministically from node_id-independent fields only (so renaming ids doesn't break byte-stability — important! use content hashes not ids in the serialized form, or exclude volatile metadata). Tokenize with the serving tokenizer. All offsets refer to this stream.

**Phase 1 — Minting.** After each append/turn/tool-result, mint anchors at allowed kinds. Placement rule: candidate offsets are node boundaries in L(T); mint if (a) distance from previous anchor ≥ δ_min (avoid churn) OR kind ∈ {TOOL_RESULT_POST, COMPACT SEAM} (always mint — these are high-edit-probability seams), and (b) block-aligned offset advanced by ≥ B tokens (else the KV gain is zero — skip, just update latest anchor's cert). Compute prefix_hash incrementally (rolling SHA-256 over blocks). Push KV blocks (engine does this automatically with prefix caching; we record the handle). Evaluate ApplicableInv(o) — but incrementally: only invariants dirtied since last anchor (readset/scope ∩ newly appended region ≠ ∅); inherit the rest from parent anchor's cert. Store cert. This is O(dirty) not O(total).

**Phase 2 — Edit ingestion.**
```
on EditEvent e:
  T' = apply(e, T)
  p = len(LCP(L(T), L(T')))         // longest common token prefix
  // structural fast path: if e targets node n and L is node-framed,
  // p = token offset of start of n's frame (precomputed at mint time as node_start[n])
  alive = { a : a.block_aligned_off <= p }
  best  = argmax_{a∈alive} a.block_aligned_off
  dead  = Anchors \ alive
  R_dirty = [p, max(|L(T)|, |L(T')|))   // conservative dirty region
  recert = { i : (scope(i) ∪ readset(i)) ∩ R_dirty ≠ ∅ }
  // lattice shortcut: drop i from recert if ∃ j ∈ recert with i ≤ j and cert_j will be re-derived;
  // evaluate maximal elements only, propagate verdicts down the Hasse diagram.
  run each i ∈ maximal(recert) on T'; propagate; collect verdicts
  if any HARD invariant fails on the *new suffix region*: quarantine edit ->
     either reject edit (restore T) or route to repair loop (policy decision, code-as-law: law wins)
  emit PrefillPlan(best, ...)
  free(dead.kv_handles subject to refcounts from other sessions' radix shares)
  T ← T'
```

Note the LCP computation cost: comparing full token streams is O(n). Optimization: compare block-by-block using stored per-block hashes at anchors and the engine's radix tree — find deepest shared radix path in O(depth). Since anchors store prefix_hash at block granularity, binary search over anchor offsets with hash comparison: O(log A) hash comparisons, each O(1) (hash equality implies byte equality w.h.p.; verify final boundary block bytes to rule out collision). Concretely: sort alive candidates descending, test largest with block_aligned_off ≤ tentative p... simpler: walk the radix tree of the engine — it already computes the shared prefix. We mirror it: `p = engine.match_prefix(tokens_of(T'))` returns matched length; then best = last anchor with block_aligned_off ≤ p. But we want to avoid tokenizing all of T′ twice; fine, tokenize once.

Edge cases to nail:
- **Edit inside a block**: p falls mid-block; effective reuse = ⌊p/B⌋·B; if that's < best.anchor.block_aligned_off, demote best to the next-lower anchor. Rule: `best = max{ a : a.block_aligned_off ≤ ⌊p/B⌋·B }`.
- **Pure append**: p = |L(T)|, all anchors alive, best = newest, suffix = delta only. This is the steady-state hot path: cost per turn = O(new tokens).
- **Compaction**: treat as REPLACE of range with SUMMARY node; seam anchor minted at c₀ with cert requiring summary-fidelity invariants (each open tool call referenced, etc.). Old anchors in [c₀, c₁) freed.
- **Rollback-to-anchor**: truncate T to a.anchor's node; all later anchors freed; suffix re-prefill from that anchor. Used when HARD invariant fails mid-generation.
- **Cross-session sharing**: radix keys are content-addressed (prefix_hash chain), so two agents with shared system prompt share KV; refcount handles; never free while refcount > 0.

**Phase 3 — Re-prefill.**
```
execute(plan):
  req.tokens = L(T')
  req.cache_prefix = plan.anchor.kv   // engine resumes attention from these blocks
  req.prefill_range = [plan.reuse_tokens, |req.tokens|)
  out = engine.decode(req)
  // post-generation: mint anchors for the new suffix at its semantic seams,
  // inheriting cert base from plan.anchor.cert minus recert'd entries plus fresh verdicts
```

Correctness argument (sketch but concrete):
- *Soundness of reuse*: attention at position t depends only on KV of positions < t; KV blocks for [0,o) were computed from exactly canon(L(T)[0,o)); ASC condition 1 guarantees L(T′)[0,o) = same bytes; transformer KV is a pure function of the token prefix (no cross-request state), therefore reuse is bit-exact equivalent to recomputation. (Caveat to state: sampling temperature/decoding params don't affect prefill KV; but if the engine fuses system prompts differently or uses sliding-window attention, window must exceed o or the anchor must respect window boundaries — add constraint: anchors only within the attention-honest region.)
- *Soundness of certification inheritance*: invariant i not in recert has (scope ∪ readset) ∩ R_dirty = ∅, so its inputs are byte-identical in T′, and predicates are deterministic functions of inputs ⇒ verdict carries over. Determinism requirement: invariant code must be pure & versioned; impure reads (clock, RNG, network) must be declared in readset as EnvRegions or the cert is marked PASS_ASSUME and expires.
- *Lattice completeness*: evaluating maximal elements of recert under ≤ suffices because verdicts propagate down (if P_j passes on S_j ⊇ S_i then P_i passes on S_i, by definition of ≤). Failures propagate up: a FAIL on narrow i forces re-eval of joins containing it.

Complexity: per edit, O(|Δ| tokens) prefill compute + O(|recert|) predicate evals + O(log A) hash comparisons for survival. Steady-state append: O(δ_min) amortized minting overhead.

### What makes it "code-as-law"

The invariants aren't documentation; they're executed on every mint and every edit, with verdicts bound into the anchor's cert by evidence digests, and HARD failures have teeth: the edit is rejected/quarantined, generation rolls back to the last anchor whose cert is fully green. The lattice isn't decorative either — it's what makes incremental enforcement sound (evaluate tops, propagate down) and what defines which certs survive an edit (readset-based dirty tracking). Law = versioned, deterministic, sandboxed code; the lattice = the partial order that lets you pay only for what the edit could possibly have broken.

### Numbers/concrete parameters (to be grounded)

- Block size B = 16 tokens (vLLM default) — state it, note it's engine param.
- δ_min = 512 tokens default; always-mint kinds override.
- Hash: SHA-256 over canonical CBOR of the token id sequence per block, chained: H_k = SHA256(H_{k−1} ‖ bytes(tokens_k)) — matches radix-tree keying.
- Keep-last-K: K=4 per kind except PINNED (session init, policy pins) and MILESTONE (kept forever within session).

### Failure modes / honesty

Must include: cache eviction by engine under memory pressure (kv_handle can dangle → detect via radix lookup miss → fall back to full prefill from nearest live lower anchor or scratch); tokenizer version drift (anchors store tokenizer_version; mismatch ⇒ all anchors invalid); attention-window constraints; nondeterministic tools making readsets undeclarable (force PASS_ASSUME + TTL); collision risk negligible but boundary-block byte verify included.
